summary.headline: JK Lakshmi Q2 FY27: EBITDA/t fell to about Rs510-520 on monsoon and shutdowns; fuel guided up to Rs2/1,000 kcal in Q3 and Rs2.15-2.2 in Q4.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 as seasonally weak, hit by heavy monsoon rains in Chhattisgarh and coastal Gujarat, planned shutdowns, and fuel cost inflation that the industry could not pass on during July-September. Fuel cost rose to Rs1.82 per 1,000 kcal in Q2 from Rs1.54, and blended power cost rose to Rs6.24/unit from Rs5.52 in Q1. Management said prices moved up from late September and in October in both trade and non-trade channels, with further hikes of about Rs10 in November and Rs10-15 in December expected. Volume growth was 5% in Q2 and about 7% in H1. The company cut its FY2030 capacity target to 25 MT from 30 MT to protect the net debt/EBITDA cap of 3.5x.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA per tonne (analyst estimate cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: Down from prior quarters; management did not dispute the figure
Expected to reach about 49% after new solar

financial_highlights.value: Rising; peak about 2.5x by end FY27 per management

segments.name: Cement (core)
segments.commentary: Volume growth 5% in Q2 and 7% in H1, with management expecting to match industry growth (7-8%) in H2. Premium product share about 27%, targeted at 27-28% (aim 30%).

segments.name: Non-cement (RMC, AAC blocks)
segments.commentary: Non-cement revenue Rs183 crore in Q2, of which RMC Rs86 crore and AAC about Rs70 crore; blended margin about 5%.

guidance_outlook: Fuel cost guidance: about Rs2 per 1,000 kcal in Q3 FY27; Rs2.15-2.2 in Q4 if current conditions persist.
Price increases of about Rs10/t in November and Rs10-15/t in December were indicated, relative to Q2 average.
Management expects to recover part of the cost increase and return EBITDA toward Rs700/t levels; it did not give a firm timeline.
Capex guidance: about Rs1,500 crore in FY27 and about Rs2,000 crore in each of the next two years; about Rs1,000 crore of FY27 capex for Durg.
Capacity target revised to 25 MT by FY2030 from 30 MT earlier, to keep net debt/EBITDA within 3.5x.
Net debt/EBITDA to remain below 3.5x; working capital release expected in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Durg (Chhattisgarh): 2.3 MT clinker and 1.6 MT cement; more than 50% civil work done; commissioning targeted by March 2028. Total spend about Rs600-650 crore to date (Rs400 crore in H1 FY27).
Madhubani (Bihar): 1.5 MT; all clearances in place; 80% piling complete; commissioning targeted by March 2028.
Prayagraj: 1.5 MT; all clearances in place; equipment ordering done; commissioning targeted by March 2028.
Northeast plant: about Rs1,800 crore capex; commissioning targeted around March 2029; four mines in Northeast; equipment ordering just starting.
Mejia (West Bengal): 1.5 MT replacing earlier Patratu plan; land and clearances available; commissioning around FY2030. Current capacity is 18 MT, rising to 22.6 MT after the East expansion.
demand_pricing: Monsoon and planned shutdowns in July-September depressed Q2 volumes and prices; prices rose from late September and in October in both trade and non-trade channels.
Non-trade margins are now as good as or better than trade in many markets, per management. Trade share has held around 58-59%.
Management said the North is a supplier market as capacity is added in Rajasthan, and that the company is consolidating in North, East and West rather than spreading thin.
Gap to UltraTech realisations about Rs300/t, mainly in North markets; company is pushing premium products to anchor base prices.
Domestic coal auction prices reportedly up more than 200%, limiting the shift to cheaper fuels.

qa_highlights.question: What are fuel cost expectations for Q3 and Q4, and what NSR trend is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel is Rs2/1,000 kcal in Q3 and Rs2.15-2.2 in Q4 if current conditions persist. Prices rose in October and are expected to rise about Rs10/t in November and Rs10-15/t in December.

qa_highlights.question: How much Durg capex has been spent and what is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs200 crore in H1 (Rs400 crore including the prior-year spend), about Rs450 crore cumulative per Arun Shukla, and Rs600-650 crore per Sudhir Bidkar. FY27 capex about Rs1,500 crore, with Rs1,000 crore for Durg; Rs2,000 crore a year for the following two years.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Northeast plant commission and what incentives apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning around March 2029. Capex about Rs1,800 crore. Incentives to be discussed separately.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company close the realisation gap with UltraTech of about Rs300/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaps have narrowed in East and West Gujarat; North still has a larger gap. Premiumisation is the main lever.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rising; what is the leverage plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt/EBITDA to stay below 3.5x. It is expected to peak around 2.5x by end FY27, with working capital release in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the FY2030 capacity target cut from 30 MT to 25 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose to avoid over-leveraging and keep net debt/EBITDA within 3.5x, prioritising balance-sheet discipline over reaching 30 MT.

risks_watch: Fuel cost volatility: management said Q4 is hard to forecast, and bag cost depends on petroleum prices.
Net debt/EBITDA rising with capex of Rs1,500-2,000 crore a year; management expects a peak around 2.5x.
Execution risk on the Durg, Madhubani, Prayagraj and Mejia projects by March 2028, and on Northeast by March 2029.
Realisation gap to UltraTech (about Rs300/t) and increased capacity in North India, including Ambuja and Shree expansions.
Whether the October-December price hikes hold through the festive period and into Q3 and Q4.
Receivable of about Rs130 crore in arbitration with no provision; management says it has a good case.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management acknowledged weak Q2 and cost pressure, but said demand and prices improved from late September and that H2 is seasonally stronger. Answers on fuel outlook, bag cost, Northeast incentives and Q4 were guarded or deferred.
key_quotes: Q4, I think is very difficult to kind of give any projection because things are so uncertain and volatile that it's very difficult to kind of forecast.
We wanted to make sure that our balance sheet does not go haywire.
Maintaining balance sheet discipline is more important than just reaching a figure of 30 by 30.
Non-trade profitability is better in some of the market, definitely, because some of the market trade prices have not gone up to that extent, right?
